name: Beaver Valley Family Park
note: Regional District of Kootenay Boundary / Beaver Valley Recreation campground about 3-5 km east of Fruitvale off Highway 3B; tent and RV sites with 30-amp electrical, water and some pull-throughs, plus toilets, hot showers, kitchen shelter, disc golf, pickleball and playground; fishing in nearby Marsh Creek. Open May long weekend to Labour Day. Reservable via the Beaver Valley Recreation office. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Approximate: May long weekend to Labour Day.
field_notes.Fees: Village of Fruitvale listing for the RDKB park: $15-20 a night per vehicle. Read 2026-10-15.

name: Toad River Lodge & RV Park
note: Historic Alaska Highway lodge (Mile 422) on Reflection Lake, Toad River. 23-site full-service RV park, pull-through & back-in, full hookups + fire rings, wifi, laundry; gas/diesel, cafe on site. Full service early May-mid Oct. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Full hookups $47.50 plus tax, early May to mid-October.

name: Lundbreck Falls Provincial Recreation Area
note: Alberta Parks PRA 25 km NW of Pincher Creek off Hwy 3 along the Crowsnest River, below Lundbreck Falls. 46 RV sites (29 powered, 17 unserviced) in two loops plus 12 walk-in tent sites; some pull-throughs. No potable water - bring your own. Reservable via Alberta Parks, open ~mid-May to Sep. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: A night: unserviced $28 (14 sites); power (15/30-amp) $36 (26 sites). Season May 8 - Sep 29. Reservable in season. GST included. The campground's Alberta Parks page (updated May 28, 2026), read 2026-10-12.

name: McLean Creek Provincial Recreation Area
note: Large Alberta Parks campground 12 km W of Bragg Creek off Hwy 66 in a foothills forest, adjacent to the McLean Creek OHV Public Land Use Zone. ~170 sites (96 powered 15/30A, 74 unserviced) across multiple loops; showers, laundry, dump station, seasonal potable water. Reservable via Alberta Parks, open year-round. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: A night: unserviced $31 (74 sites); power (15/30-amp) $39 (96 sites). Open year-round. Reservable in season. GST included. The campground's Alberta Parks page (updated Sep 24, 2026), read 2026-10-12.

name: Oldman Dam PRA - Castleview Campground
note: Alberta Parks fully-serviced campground in Oldman Dam PRA, 13 km N of Pincher Creek on Hwy 785 by the Oldman River/Reservoir. 29 sites with power/water/sewer (15/30A) and privacy partitions, showers and dump station, RVs to ~50 ft. Reservable via Alberta Parks, open ~May-Sep. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: A night: power, water and sewer (15/30-amp) $45 (29 sites). Season May 15 - Sep 30. Reservable in season. GST included. The campground's Alberta Parks page (updated Jul 8, 2026), read 2026-10-12.

name: Cypress Hills Provincial Park - Elkwater Campground
note: Cypress Hills PP, in the Elkwater townsite near Elkwater Lake. 72 RV-friendly sites in open mixed forest, most power/water (15/30 amp); flush toilets, showers, playground, walking trails to the waterfront. Loop C stays open year-round (weather permitting). Reservable via Alberta Parks (ABPP, 90 days out). --Claude

field_notes.Season: Loop C stays open year-round (weather permitting); the other loops close Oct 11. Water is shut off for the winter.
field_notes.Fees: A night: power and water (15/30-amp) $47 (70 sites). Season Jan 1 - Oct 11. Reservable in season. GST included. The campground's Alberta Parks page (updated Apr 24, 2026), read 2026-10-12.

name: Cypress Hills Provincial Park - Firerock Campground
note: Cypress Hills PP, on the west side of Elkwater Lake (loop confirmed on satellite at 49.6628,-110.3149). ~126 sites: ~65 unserviced and ~61 powered (15/30 amp); firepits, flush toilets, showers, boat launch, playground. Upper loop treed; lower loop open meadow near the water. RV or tent, drive-in. Reservable via Alberta Parks (ABPP, 90 days out). --Claude

field_notes.Fees: A night: unserviced $31 (65 sites); power (15/30-amp) $39 (61 sites). Season May 13 - Oct 11. Reservable in season. GST included. The campground's Alberta Parks page (updated May 28, 2026), read 2026-10-12.

name: Wildhorse Lake Provincial Recreation Area — Kinky Lake Campground
note: Alberta Parks PRA campground (operated by West Fraser Mills under contract) about 25 km SW of Hinton off Hwy 16. 10 unserviced sites suitable for RVs and tents, close lake access on Kinky Lake; pit toilets, water pump. Open ~May 1–Oct 31, reservable via the operator; RV access can be limited at the shoulder edges of the season. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: A night: unserviced $25 (10 sites). Season May 1 - Oct 31. Reservable in season. GST included. The campground's Alberta Parks page (updated Apr 20, 2026), read 2026-10-12.

name: Wildhorse Lake Provincial Recreation Area — Wildhorse Lake Campground
note: Alberta Parks PRA campground (operated by West Fraser Mills under contract) SW of Hinton. 19 drive-up unserviced sites plus 3 walk-in tent sites; no hookups; pit toilets, water pump. Open ~May 1–Oct 31, reservable via the operator. Distinct from Kinky Lake campground in the same PRA. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: A night: unserviced $25 (19 sites). Season May 1 - Oct 31. Reservable in season. GST included. The campground's Alberta Parks page (updated Apr 20, 2026), read 2026-10-12.

name: Fish Lake Provincial Recreation Area — Fish Lake Campground
note: Alberta Parks campground on Fish (Shunda) Lake, 6 km W of Nordegg off Hwy 11. ~104 sites: 80 unserviced and 24 powered, incl. pull-through and lakeside sites, plus a group site; boat launch, laundry, store, fish-cleaning station, drinking water. Reservable via Alberta Parks, ~May 1–Oct 14. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: A night: unserviced $28 (79 sites); power (15/20-amp) $36 (21 sites). Season May 8 - Oct 4. Reservable in season. GST included. The campground's Alberta Parks page (updated May 27, 2026), read 2026-10-12.

name: Seven Mile Campground (Seven Mile Provincial Recreation Area)
note: Alberta Parks PRA in the Clearwater River valley, 48 km SW of Caroline on Hwy 591. Drive-in sites (RV+tent), cook shelter, firepits; bring your own water. Self-managed by Friends of the Eastern Slopes Association; $30 annual membership encouraged. OHV staging area; used by hikers and horseback riders but has no equestrian facilities. Bear country. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: No nightly fee: the Friends of the Eastern Slopes Association runs it and asks campers to buy an annual membership. Open year-round. First come, first served. The campground's Alberta Parks page (updated Jun 8, 2026), read 2026-10-12.

name: Dry Island Buffalo Jump Provincial Park - Tolman East Campground
note: East-bank Red Deer River valley campground in Dry Island Buffalo Jump PP, near Tolman Bridge (~33 km south of the park day-use area). 40 unserviced sites tucked under cottonwoods, sheltered, suitable for tents and RVs; hand boat launch, playground, pit/vault toilets, water pump, no firewood. Vehicle access closed mid-Oct to mid-May. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Approximate: Vehicle access closed mid-October to mid-May.
field_notes.Fees: A night: unserviced $25 (40 sites). Season May 15 - Oct 14. First come, first served. GST included. The campground's Alberta Parks page (updated Sep 28, 2026), read 2026-10-12.

name: Dry Island Buffalo Jump Provincial Park - Tolman West Campground
note: West-bank campground in Dry Island Buffalo Jump PP at Tolman Bridge on the Red Deer River. 25 large open unserviced sites well suited to RVs; cooking shelter, fire pits, hand launch, pit/vault toilets, water pump, no firewood. Vehicle access closed mid-Oct to mid-May. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Approximate: Vehicle access closed mid-October to mid-May.
field_notes.Fees: A night: unserviced $25 (25 sites). Season May 15 - Oct 14. First come, first served. GST included. The campground's Alberta Parks page (updated Oct 7, 2026), read 2026-10-12.

name: Moose Lake Provincial Park
note: Alberta Parks provincial park on Moose Lake, N of Bonnyville near Glendon. 59 drive-in sites, 47 with 15/30-amp power; picnic tables, firewood, toilets, sewage dump, boat launch, sandy beach. Open May-Oct, reservable online. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: A night: unserviced $22 (11 sites); power (15/30-amp) $30 (47 sites). Season May 14 - Sep 8. Reservable in season. GST included. The campground's Alberta Parks page (updated Apr 23, 2026), read 2026-10-12.

name: Beaver Lake Provincial Recreation Area
note: Alberta Parks recreation area on Beaver Lake, 6 km SE of Lac La Biche off Hwy 881. 89 sites: 15 full-service (power/water/sewer), 59 powered, 15 unserviced; shower house, flush + vault toilets, playground, beach, boat launch, store. Dump station in nearby Lac La Biche. Reservable online. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: A night: unserviced $32 (15 sites); power (15/30-amp) $38 (59 sites); power, water and sewer (15/30-amp) $54 (15 sites). Season May 14 - Sep 8. Reservable in season. GST included. The campground's Alberta Parks page (updated Aug 17, 2026), read 2026-10-12.

name: Notikewin Provincial Park
note: Alberta Parks provincial park at the Notikewin–Peace river confluence, 35 km N of Manning then ~30 km E on Hwy 692. Treed drive-in sites; bring own water. Caution: Alberta Parks warns the access and internal roads are narrow and heavily wooded and not suited to larger RVs/motorhomes; the lower loop and boat launch are currently closed due to a road failure (upper loop open). --Claude

field_notes.Season: The lower loop and the boat launch are closed until further notice after a road failure; the upper loop is open first-come.
field_notes.Fees: A night: unserviced $20 (19 sites). Season May 14 - Sep 7. First come, first served. GST included. The campground's Alberta Parks page (updated Aug 11, 2026), read 2026-10-12.

name: Calaway RV Park & Campground
note: Privately-run campground at Calaway Park amusement park west of Calgary off Trans-Canada Hwy 1. 100+ sites: 56 full-service, 41 partial (power), 7 unserviced/tent; pull-through and back-in, coin laundry, showers. Open weekends mid-May then daily early Jun-early Sep; reservable online or by phone. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Approximate: Weekends from mid-May, then daily early June to early September.
field_notes.Fees: Full service plus GST: $52-62 (Stampede $57-67); power only $48.

name: Nature's Hideaway Family Campground
note: 30-acre private family campground on the Highwood River near De Winton, ~30 min SE of Calgary; fully-serviced RV sites (grass or gravel) among cottonwoods with river/tubing and beach access. Seasonal Apr 15-Oct 15, 2-night minimum on weekends (3 on long weekends), reservable online. --Claude  MINIMUM STAY: 2 nights on regular weekends, 3 on long weekends; none midweek (naturesfamilycampground.com, 2026-10-12). --Claude

Booking: min stay 2 nights on weekends, 3 on holidays

field_notes.Booking: 2 nights on regular weekends, 3 on long weekends (operator's rates page).
field_notes.Fees: Before GST, 2 adults: water + power 20A C$47, full service C$55; unserviced C$41.

name: Red Deer Lions Campground
note: Lions-club campground on the Red Deer River right in the city of Red Deer, on the trail network. Serviced sites from 15-amp power-only to 30-amp and 50-amp full hookup, plus unserviced and no-service overflow sites. Reservable, stays up to 28 days. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Red Deer Lions: full hookup 30-amp $52.50-55 plus GST, 50-amp premium $65, 15-amp power only $40. Read 2026-10-15.

name: Tyrrell Lake Recreation Site
note: Rustic provincial recreation site on the south shore of Tyrrell Lake, ~20 km NW of Creighton via Highway 106 (Hanson Lake Road); drive-in gravel access road off the highway. 6 non-electrical sites plus a boat launch; RVs/trailers visible in the loop on satellite. Sask Parks Pass required; managed by the Narrow Hills office. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Self-registration, first come, first served. Sask Parks' 2026-27 fee table charges an unserviced site $18 (economy) or $20 (non-electrical) a night, taxes included; which class this campground is isn't published. Plus a vehicle entry permit, $11 a day ($42 a week, $82 a year; free for Saskatchewan residents 65 and older). AWH 2026-10-12: 'For the 6 SK sites you might as well just say $18-$20.'

name: Nokomis City Park
note: Town of Nokomis municipal campground on the north edge of town along Hwy 20. Town page: ~20 sites, non-electrical, 15-amp and 30-amp electric; sheltered camp kitchen, potable water, outdoor toilets, dump station. Open May 31-Oct 1. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Town of Nokomis: 15- or 30-amp sites $20 a day, non-electric $10. Read 2026-10-15.

name: Notukeu Regional Park
note: SK regional park (local authority) adjacent to Ponteix beside Notukeu Creek, by the pool/spray park and golf course. 17 full-service 30-amp RV sites, 13 sites with water and 15-amp, plus a tenting area. Open May long weekend to end of September. FCFS on arrival; reservations by phone/email take precedence. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Approximate: May long weekend to the end of September.

name: Oungre Memorial Regional Park
note: SK regional park (local authority) near Oungre. 75 sites, accepts big rigs; electric sites, water, showers, dump station, plus 9-hole golf, mini-golf, sports courts and an indoor aquatic centre. Open May-September (fall camping by request). Reservable. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Approximate: Open May to September (fall camping by request).
field_notes.Fees: Oungre Memorial Regional Park: full service $40 a night, 30-amp $33, 15-amp $28, tents $25. Read 2026-10-15.

name: Michel Point Campground & RV Park
note: Privately-operated campground on the Michel Point peninsula within the Dore Lake (provincial) Recreation Site in northern Saskatchewan. Serviced drive-in sites: power/water and power/water/sewer, plus non-potable fill, sewage dump, boat launch, fish-cleaning shack and a ~3-km sand beach. Nightly, monthly and seasonal sites (transient welcome); open May long weekend to Sep 30; book by phone/Facebook. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: 'Power & Water: $35/night'; 'Power, Water & Sewer: $45/night' (30-amp sites; 'Site rates include 4 adults'), the same nightly rates as its 2025 list; monthly and seasonal rates too. Open May long weekend to September 30. Its rates page, read 2026-10-12.

name: Lundar Beach Provincial Park
note: On the east shore of Lake Manitoba, 19 km W of PTH 6 on PR 419. One campground, 33 drive-in sites (26 with 30-amp electric, 7 basic), flush toilets, showers, sani-dump, sandy beach, 3.2-km marsh trail. Open mid-May-Sept long weekend; reservable via goingtocamp. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Approximate: Mid-May to the September long weekend.
field_notes.Fees: A night: basic (no hookups) $13.65; electric $19.95, GST included, the same every night of the week. Plus a $10 reservation fee per booking, and each vehicle needs a provincial park vehicle permit ($9.50 a day, $16.50 for three days, $44.50 a year). Manitoba Parks' booking site (July 2027 nights) and 2026 fees, read 2026-10-12.
